---
title: "How do I calculate the proportion below a cutoff in a normal model?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I calculate the proportion below a cutoff in a normal model?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Identify mean, positive standard deviation, and cutoff.

2. Run pnorm(cutoff,mean,sd).

3. Translate the returned number into an area or proportion.

## Runnable example

```{r}
mu <- 100; sigma <- 15; cutoff <- 85
answer <- pnorm(cutoff,mean=mu,sd=sigma)
print(answer)
```

## Interpret the result

The modeled probability below 85 is about 0.159 (15.9%) when the mean is 100 and standard deviation is 15.

## Check before using your own data

A standard deviation must be positive and the assumed normal model must suit the real variable.
